The most likely corrupted element is **Rf**. Its value of 22.16 kΩ caps the transimpedance. With loop gain A much larger than 1, Zt ≈ Rf·A/(1+A), so Zt can't exceed Rf. The measured 86.71 dBΩ matches 20·log10(22.16 kΩ) = 86.9 dBΩ almost exactly. Reaching 102 dBΩ requires about 158 kΩ or more. Rf also sets the thermal noise floor: at 1 MHz, sqrt(4kT/Rf) ≤ 540 fA/√Hz needs Rf ≳ 57 kΩ, so 22 kΩ alone exceeds the noise spec before any amplifier noise is added.

Input device M1 is the second candidate, since its gm sets the amplifier gain and input noise. Its bias current is set by the M2 mirror, which makes M2 the third candidate.
